title: Taking a message
goal: Pass on news with -mIş and requests with -mA + possessive: Yarın gelecekmiş; Erken gelmeni söyledi.

intro.text: To pass something on, add `-mIş` to the verb: *Ali yarın gelecekmiş* (Ali says he's coming tomorrow). To pass on a request, use `-mA` + possessive + accusative and *söylemek*: *Erken gelmeni söyledi* (She told you to come early).

vocab.en: to say hello (to someone), to send your regards

exercises.question: Ali said: *“Yarın geleceğim.”* How do you pass it on?

why.1: When you pass it on, Ali's **I** becomes **he**: *gelecekmiş*.
why.2: *Geldi* is a plain past, **he came**. Ali was talking about tomorrow.

exercises.explain: *gel-ecek-miş*: the future, plus `-mIş` for what you were told.

exercises.en: Murat called: the meeting's been postponed, he says.

reject.why: *Ertelendi* gives it as your own news. **He says** points to `-mIş`: *ertelenmiş*.

exercises.explain: *ertele-n-miş*: the passive *-n*, then `-mIş` for news you heard from Murat.

exercises.label: Before *söyledi*: she told me to come, you to come… (`-mA` + possessive + accusative)
exercises.explain: The possessive names who is to come: *gel-me-m-i* (me), *gel-me-n-i* (you), *gel-me-s-i-n-i* (him, her)… then *söyledi*.

exercises.prompt: My mother told me to come home early.
accept: Annem bana eve erken gelmemi söyledi.

reject.why: *Gelmesini* is **for him or her to come**. For **me**: *gelmemi*.

exercises.en: The teacher told us to open our books.

accept: Apparently Ayşe is ill and will not come to work today.
Apparently Ayşe is [sick|ill] and [is not going to come|is not coming|will not be coming] to work today.
Apparently Ayşe is sick and will not come to work today.
Ayşe is [ill|sick], apparently; she [will not come|is not coming|is not going to come|will not be coming] to work today.
[I hear|I heard|They say] Ayşe is [ill|sick] and [will not come|is not coming|is not going to come|will not be coming] to work today.

exercises.prompt: The manager wants us to finish the report by tomorrow.
exercises.text: Müdür raporu yarına kadar bitirmemizi istiyor.
accept: Müdür yarına kadar raporu bitirmemizi istiyor.

exercises.question: What does Elif want Deniz to do?

context.tr: Hayır, dışarı çıktı. Mesaj bırakmak ister misin?
context.en: No, he's gone out. Would you like to leave a message?

context.tr: Evet. Yarınki toplantı iptal edilmiş. Beni geri aramasını söyler misin?
context.en: Yes. Tomorrow's meeting has been cancelled. Could you tell him to call me back?

options: Tell Can to call her back

why.1: The meeting has already been cancelled: *iptal edilmiş*, Elif heard it from someone.

exercises.explain: *Beni geri aramasını söyler misin?*: `-mA` + the possessive of Can (*-sı*) + accusative, **tell him to call me back**.

exercises.text: Doktor bana iki gün dinlen___ söyledi.
exercises.en: The doctor told me to rest for two days.

reject.why: *Dinlenmesini* is for **him** or **her**; the doctor told **me**: *dinlenmemi*.
A request needs `-mA` + possessive + accusative, which names who is to rest: *dinlenmemi*.

exercises.explain: *dinlen-me-m-i söyledi*: the possessive *-m* names you as the one who should rest.

accept: I told you not to be late!
I had told you not to be late!
I did tell you not to be late!

exercises.question: *Annem diyor ki akşama misafir gelecekmiş.* What does the speaker know?
options: Her mother says guests are coming this evening

why.1: `-mIş` shows she heard it from her mother; she didn't invite anyone.
why.2: *Gelecekmiş* is the future: they are still to come.

exercises.explain: *Diyor ki* names the source, and `-mIş` passes on what was said: *gel-ecek-miş*.

exercises.prompt: Apparently the shop is closed on Sundays.

reject.why: Without `-mIş` this is your own knowledge. **Apparently** points to news you heard: *kapalıymış*.
